title: Switching-lemma depth bound for bounded-depth circuits
statement:
Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $n \ge 1$ variables with depth at most $d$, size at most $s$, and maximum fan-in at most $w$, where $d \ge 2$ and $s, w, l > 0$. Fix a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ and natural numbers $l, t$ satisfying $s \cdot \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} \le \varepsilon/2$ and $\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{t} \le \varepsilon/2$, and put
\[
  \delta \;=\; \frac{1}{40w}\left(\frac{1}{40l}\right)^{d-2}.
\]
Draw a random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables by leaving each coordinate free with probability $\delta$ and otherwise fixing it to a uniformly random Boolean value, all coordinates independent. Let $c\!\restriction_{\rho}$ denote the restricted function of the free coordinates, obtained by evaluating $c$ with the coordinates set by $\rho$ held to their fixed values. Then the probability that $c\!\restriction_{\rho}$ has decision-tree depth exceeding $t$—that is, that no decision tree of depth at most $t$ computes it—satisfies
\[
  \Pr_{\rho}\!\left[\, \operatorname{depth}_{\mathrm{DT}}\!\left(c\!\restriction_{\rho}\right) > t \,\right]
  \;\le\; \varepsilon \;+\; s \cdot \exp\!\left(-\frac{n}{120\,w}\right)
  \;+\; s \cdot \exp\!\left(-\frac{n}{120\,l}\right).
\]

replaced:
Let $c$ be a circuit on $n$ variables with $n > 0$, depth at most $d$, size at most
$s$, and fan-in at most $w$, where $d \ge 2$ and $s, w, l > 0$. Fix $\varepsilon > 0$ and
naturals $l, t$ with $s \cdot \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^l \le \varepsilon/2$ and
$\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^t \le \varepsilon/2$. Then under a Bernoulli($\mathrm{composedDelta}\,w\,l\,d$)
restriction $\rho$,
\[
  \Pr\!\left[\, \mathrm{DT}(c\!\restriction_\rho) > t \,\right]
  \le \varepsilon + s \cdot \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n}{120 w}\right)
  + s \cdot \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n}{120 l}\right).
\]
The exponential tails vanish as $n \to \infty$, giving $\Pr \le \varepsilon$ asymptotically.
